episode.episode: Philips Hue: The smart home’s light bulb moment
episode.showDescription: Version History is a show about the best gadgets ever. And the worst ones. And the ones that might have changed the world, if they ever actually shipped. Every week, your favorite people from The Verge and beyond hang out to tell and debate the story of a gadget, app, website, or any other tech product, and try to determine the item’s true legacy. Because not every product is a hit, but every product has a story. And the ones that really matter aren’t always the ones you think. From the Verge and the Vox Media Podcast Network.
episode.episodeDescription: The humble light bulb might be the ultimate success story in the smart home. Our connected, adaptable homes are supposed to be customizable, connected to everything, and incredibly easy to use, and nothing has made that work quite like Philips Hue lights. In this episode, The Verge's David Pierce and Jennifer Pattison Tuohy are joined by smart home journalist and expert Richard Gunther to tell the Hue's story. We trace the product's history from its origins in the smartphone revolution, try to figure out how Philips managed to turn a staggeringly expensive lightbulb into a must-have gadget, and look at whether there's even more invention left in the future of lighting. We’re also on video! Check us out on YouTube. Subscribe to The Verge for unlimited access to theverge.com, subscriber-exclusive newsletters, and our ad-free podcast feed. We love hearing from you! transcript_window.text: And I remember, especially in those early days when Alexa, Google Assistant, and then HomeKit were all really on the come up.
They were all so different that I feel like I spent a lot of my time, and I'm sure you both spent a lot of your time, just explaining to people what worked with what.
Yeah.
And having Hue just be a yes was such an unbelievable victory that it was like, I actually don't have to ask about all the other things in your house.
These bulbs will work.
They will work.
Yes, they're expensive.
They will work.
And that was so meaningful for so, and in many ways still is so meaningful.
I think that's a good one.
The only other one I had was this peak smartphone excitement, which I think like there's a real moment in 2012 that that's kind of happening anyway.
This is like Instagram is starting to come up.
Social media has not turned on us yet in any sort of meaningful cultural way.
But I think just thinking back to all of these demos and the idea that I could take out my phone and control my lights was so futuristic and mind blowing to so many people.
That part of me is like there's a moment in that that is like my smartphone is now not just a digital device.
It is my conduit to the universe.
And it's like there's something so powerful about that that I remember experiencing for the first time.
And like I just I almost want the Hue lights to be peak smartphone.
It feels like a reach.
We had an iPad.
The iPad just came out, right?
So, yeah, it was like, but this was right when people were starting to actually buy them.
So, I mean, I would argue it was peak iPad.
Oh, interesting.
finally gave you a use for your iPad because this was the problem.
